title: Example meal and exercise plan
subtitle: An example plan for three people (Alex, Sam and Riley). Weeks 1 and 3 include a 2-week stock-up of pantry and freezer items. Prices are rough estimates for Coles in Australia.

Pantry (buy once for these 2 weeks): Weet-Bix Bites Mixed Berry (about 500 g box) × 2

meals.dinner: Turkey and bean chilli with rice
Red lentil and sweet potato curry

recipes.name: Yoghurt bowl
steps: Spoon the yoghurt into bowls.
Top with the oats and berries (straight from frozen, or thaw them for a minute in the microwave for a juicier bowl).
Add a little honey if you like. Banana slices are a good extra on your bowl.
recipes.kid: Plain yoghurt with a few berries on the side. Oats are optional.
others: Also on Thu breakfast, Sun breakfast: same amounts.

recipes.name: Tuna salad
steps: Drain the tuna and flake it into a bowl.
Chop the tomato and mix it in with the spinach and a squeeze of lime.
Serve with the bread, toasted if you like.
others: Sat lunch: use about 1.4× these amounts

recipes.name: Turkey and bean chilli with rice
recipes.makes: dinner for 3 plus lunch for 2 adults tomorrow
recipes.leftoverStep: Pack the leftovers into a container for tomorrow's lunch and refrigerate once cool.
steps: Rinse the rice and simmer it covered in double its volume of water for 12 to 15 minutes. Rest 5 minutes.
Fry the diced onion in a little oil for 3 minutes. Add the mince and break it up until browned (5 to 6 minutes).
Stir in the taco seasoning, diced tomatoes and drained beans.
Simmer on low for 15 minutes, stirring now and then.
Serve over the rice.
recipes.kid: Mince and rice served separately, with the sauce on the side.

recipes.name: Eggs on toast
steps: Toast the bread.
Scramble or fry the eggs in a little oil on medium heat (2 to 3 minutes).
Wilt the spinach in the pan for the last 30 seconds for the adults, then pile onto the toast.
recipes.kid: Plain scrambled egg on toast, no spinach.
others: Also on Sat breakfast: same amounts.

recipes.name: Sausage and bean casserole
steps: Brown the sliced sausages in a pot with the onion for 5 minutes.
Add the diced carrot, tomatoes, drained beans and half a can of water.
Simmer 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick.

recipes.name: Overnight oats
steps: The night before, stir the oats, milk and yoghurt together in a container.
Grate in the apple, stir, cover and refrigerate overnight.
Serve cold, or warm in the microwave for 1 to 2 minutes. Top yours with banana slices.
recipes.kid: Plain oats and milk, with the apple left out if she prefers.
others: Also on Fri breakfast: same amounts.

recipes.name: Chicken and yoghurt wraps
steps: Cook the chicken in a little oil for 6 to 8 minutes per side until no pink remains (or use leftover cooked chicken). Rest, then slice.
Spread yoghurt on each wrap and add the chicken, spinach and sliced cucumber.
Roll up tightly and cut in half.
recipes.kid: A plain chicken and cheese wrap if she prefers.
others: Sun lunch: use about 1.4× these amounts

recipes.name: Baked chicken nuggets and wedges
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Cut the potatoes into wedges, toss with oil and salt and roast on a tray for 35 minutes.
Cut the chicken into nugget-sized pieces.
Beat the eggs in one bowl and put the breadcrumbs in another. Dip the chicken in egg, then crumbs.
Place on a lined tray and drizzle or spray with oil. Bake 15 to 18 minutes, turning once, until golden and cooked through.
Serve with the wedges and cucumber sticks or peas.
recipes.kid: One of her favourites. Serve the nuggets and wedges plain.

recipes.name: Egg and spinach wraps
steps: Scramble the eggs (2 to 3 minutes).
Fill the wraps with egg, spinach and sliced cucumber.
Roll up and serve.

recipes.name: Turkey and lentil bolognese
recipes.makes: dinner for 3 plus lunch for 2 adults tomorrow
recipes.leftoverStep: Pack the leftovers into a container for tomorrow's lunch and refrigerate once cool.
steps: Cook the pasta in boiling salted water for 10 to 12 minutes and drain.
Fry the onion for 3 minutes, then add the mince and brown it.
Add the diced tomatoes and drained lentils and simmer 15 minutes.
Spoon the sauce over the pasta.
recipes.kid: Plain pasta with a little butter, sauce on the side.

recipes.name: Wrap pizzas
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C.
Spread passata over the wraps on trays, then top with mozzarella and sliced capsicum.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and the edges are crisp.

recipes.name: Red lentil and sweet potato curry
steps: Cook the rice.
Fry the curry paste in a little oil for 1 minute. Add the diced sweet potato, red lentils, coconut milk and a can of water.
Simmer 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils and sweet potato are soft.
Serve over the rice.
recipes.kid: Rice with a little sweet potato and the sauce on the side. A plain-rice and cheese slice dinner is fine too.

recipes.name: Butter chicken and rice
steps: Cook the rice.
Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces and brown it in a little oil for 5 minutes.
Add the butter chicken sauce and a splash of water. Simmer 12 to 15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the peas for the last 3 minutes, then finish with the yoghurt.
Serve over the rice.
recipes.kid: One of her favourites. Serve as normal, with the rice separate if she likes.

recipes.name: Weet-Bix Bites with milk
steps: Tip the Weet-Bix Bites into a bowl.
Pour over cold milk, or warm milk for a softer bowl.
others: Also on Tue breakfast, Wed breakfast, Thu breakfast, Fri breakfast, Sat breakfast, Sun breakfast: same amounts.

adult1.focus: Week 1: Getting started. Short, easy sessions to build the habit
targets: Morning: easy cardio such as a walk, bike or row. You should be able to talk in full sentences.
Afternoon: strength on Mon, Wed and Fri, 2 sets of each exercise, stopping 3 to 4 reps before you could not do another.
Saturday: a longer easy session. Sunday: rest.

days.afternoon: Strength A: Squat, press, hinge (about 50 min)

days.morning: Workout D: Easy rowing, 25 minutes steady.
days.afternoon: Optional: Workout E mobility and core, 20 minutes (or rest).
Strength B: Glutes, pull, arms (about 50 min)

days.morning: Workout F: Easy walk, 30 minutes, or an easy ride, 30 minutes.
days.afternoon: Optional: Workout E mobility and core, 20 minutes (or rest).
Strength C: Full body and carries (about 50 min)

days.session: Workout G: Pool, steady laps with short rests, 45 minutes.

targets: A 30 minute walk on 4 days this week, at a pace where you can still chat.
10 minutes of stretching after two of the walks.

days.session: Rest or an easy 15 minute walk.
Walk, 30 minutes, then 10 minutes of stretching.
Walk, 30 minutes, then 10 minutes of stretching.

workouts.name: Strength A: Squat, press, hinge (about 50 min)
items: Warm-up (5 minutes): easy rowing or a brisk walk, then arm circles, cat-cow × 8 and 8 slow bodyweight squats.
Goblet squat: hold one 10 to 12.5 kg dumbbell at your chest, 3 × 8 to 10. Start with bodyweight or a lighter dumbbell, to a comfortable depth.
Dumbbell bench press: 2 × 10 to 12.5 kg, 3 × 8 to 12. Lower slowly, press up.
Romanian deadlift (dumbbells): 2 × 10 to 12.5 kg, 3 × 8 to 10. Hinge at the hips with a flat back and soft knees.
Seated overhead press: 2 × 7 to 10 kg, 3 × 8 to 10.
Calf raise: 3 × 12 to 15, slow up and down. Hold a dumbbell once it feels easy.
Plank: 3 × 30 to 45 seconds.
Cool-down: the stretch routine below, focusing on whatever you worked.

workouts.name: Strength B: Glutes, pull, arms (about 50 min)
items: Warm-up (5 minutes): easy rowing or a brisk walk, then arm circles, cat-cow × 8 and 8 slow bodyweight squats.
Hip thrust: shoulders on the flat bench, the 7 kg bar with discs across your hips (start with the bar and add small discs), 3 × 8 to 12. A pad or folded towel on the bar helps.
Chest-supported row: lie face down on the bench, 2 × 10 to 12.5 kg, 3 × 10 to 12.
One-arm dumbbell row: 10 to 12.5 kg, 3 × 10 each side.
Push-ups: hands on the bench to make them easier, 3 sets stopping 2 reps short of failure.
Dumbbell curl (bicep curl): 2 × 7 to 10 kg, 3 × 10 to 12.
Overhead triceps extension: one 7 to 10 kg dumbbell in both hands, 3 × 10 to 12.
Dead bug: 3 × 8 each side. Then bird dog: 3 × 8 each side.
Cool-down: the stretch routine below, focusing on whatever you worked.

workouts.name: Strength C: Full body and carries (about 50 min)
items: Warm-up (5 minutes): easy rowing or a brisk walk, then arm circles, cat-cow × 8 and 8 slow bodyweight squats.
Squats: bodyweight or holding a dumbbell, 3 × 10 to 12, slow on the way down.
Dumbbell bench press: 3 × 8 to 12.
One-arm dumbbell row: 3 × 10 each side.
Romanian deadlift (dumbbells): 3 × 8 to 10.
Hammer curl: 2 × 7 to 10 kg, 3 × 10 to 12.
Farmer's carry: a 10 to 12.5 kg dumbbell in each hand, walk 30 to 40 steps, 3 rounds. Stand tall and walk at a steady pace.
Mountain climber: 3 rounds of 20 seconds on, 40 seconds rest, kept slow and controlled. Skip it if anything hurts.
Cool-down: the stretch routine below, focusing on whatever you worked.

workouts.name: Workout D: Rowing (low impact cardio)
items: Rowing machine technique: damper at 3 to 5. Use smooth strokes and gentle leg drive. Shorten the stroke if your body complains.
Easy weeks (Week 1 and 4): steady and easy for the whole session. Keep it at an easy, chatty pace.

Build weeks (Week 2 and 3): easy for 5 minutes, then repeat the number of efforts listed for the day: 2 minutes moderate (breathing harder but still in control), then 1 minute easy. Finish with easy rowing.
Stop and swap to the walk or pool if anything hurts.
Finish with the stretch routine below, focusing on calves, hip flexors, hamstrings and glutes.

workouts.name: Workout F: Easy walk or bike (steady cardio)
items: Walk on your local walking path or ride the bike path on the flat. Keep it easy, at a pace where you can chat.
Start with 5 minutes at an easier pace, then settle in. A 5 km walk takes about 55 minutes at an easy pace.
Add about 5 minutes a week. This steady work is what builds your aerobic base.
If your body complains above 3 out of 10, switch to the pool or shorten the session.
Finish with the stretch routine below, focusing on calves, hip flexors, hamstrings and glutes.

workouts.name: Workout G: Pool laps (steady cardio)
items: Swim continuous easy laps in short blocks, for example 5 to 8 minutes, with 30 seconds rest between blocks.
Keep the pace comfortable, at a level you could keep up for a long time.
Add a block every week or two. Water walking is a good swap on a sore day.
Finish with the stretch routine below, focusing on calves, hip flexors, hamstrings and glutes.

workouts.name: Workout E: Mobility and core (mat)
items: Cat-cow: 10 reps, then child's pose for 30 seconds.
Hip flexor stretch (half-kneeling, or standing if kneeling hurts): 30 to 45 seconds each side.
Figure-4 glute stretch: lying on your back, 30 to 45 seconds each side.
Thoracic twist: lying on your side (open book), 8 reps each side.
Dead bug: 8 reps each side.
Bird dog: 8 reps each side.
Side plank: 20 to 30 seconds each side.
Finish with 2 minutes of slow breathing on your back with your knees bent.

workouts.name: Stretch routine (after training, 8 to 10 minutes)
items: Hold each stretch for 30 seconds (each side where it applies), breathing slowly. You should feel a gentle pull, never pain. If your body complains, ease off or skip that stretch.
Hip flexor stretch: half-kneeling (use a pad under the knee) or standing with one foot on a step, tuck your tailbone and lean forward slightly.
Figure-4 glute stretch: lying on your back with one ankle on the opposite knee, pull the knee toward your chest.
Hamstring stretch: lying on your back with a towel looped around one foot and the leg raised, keeping the knee slightly soft.
Calf stretch: hands on a wall, one leg back with the heel down, knee straight. Then bend the knee a little to reach the lower calf.
Quad stretch: standing, hold on to something, pull one heel toward your glute with the knees together.
Doorway chest stretch: forearm on the door frame, step through gently.
Child's pose: 30 to 45 seconds, arms stretched forward.
Thoracic twist: lying on your side with knees bent, rotate the top arm open, 8 reps each side.

notes: If a session feels too hard, do less rather than skipping it. Consistency matters more than effort.
medical: This is an example plan. It may be worth checking with a doctor or physio before starting a new exercise plan, especially with any injury or health condition.
Consider stopping and getting checked if you notice chest pain, dizziness, or sharp or shooting pain.

notes: Walk on flat ground to start. Good shoes help more than anything else.
